text:
Justin Faulk is past 1,000 games and still eating minutes. Detroit has him at nearly 21 a night this season and more than 22 over his last ten games, up almost two and a half. He has 9 points in 22 games, with three on the power play, and 34 blocked shots.

The last two weeks have been quiet. He's gone six straight games without a point, and unlike some of the droughts on this site, the chances have thinned out too: our numbers don't call this one due. His own shooting is running a little hot, 3 goals on 1.4 expected, while the team has scored about four and a half fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. Those two things roughly cancel.

At five on five the Red Wings take about 52% of the expected goals with him out there, a bit better than without him. Evolving-Hockey's read from last season was blunt: offense isn't his game, with his team creating fewer chances with him on than with all but 4% of defensemen. He's a minutes-and-blocks defenseman on a team that has lost seven of its last ten, and that workload is the thing we'd watch.
headline: Justin Faulk, big minutes and a thin stretch
